forms.label: ている past polite
forms.negative: ぼけていませんでした

definitions.explanation: to become senile; to have one's mental faculties decline with age
for an image or photo to be out of focus or blurred
to play dumb; to feign ignorance; to act confused (often in comedy)

examples.japanese: {祖父|そふ}は{最近|さいきん}ぼけてきた。
examples.english: My grandfather has been becoming senile lately.

examples.japanese: {年|とし}をとってもぼけないように{頭|あたま}を{使|つか}おう。
examples.english: Let's keep our minds active so we don't become senile even as we age.

examples.japanese: ぼけ{防止|ぼうし}のために{毎日|まいにち}パズルを{解|と}いている。
examples.english: I solve puzzles every day to prevent senility.

examples.japanese: {写真|しゃしん}がぼけている。
{背景|はいけい}をぼけさせると{被写体|ひしゃたい}が{引|ひ}き{立|た}つ。
examples.english: Blurring the background makes the subject stand out.

examples.japanese: ピントがぼけてうまく{撮|と}れなかった。
examples.english: The focus was off and I couldn't get a good shot.

examples.japanese: ぼけないでちゃんと{答|こた}えて。
{漫才|まんざい}でぼけを{担当|たんとう}する。
examples.english: To play the funny man role in manzai comedy.

examples.japanese: ぼけとツッコミの{掛|か}け{合|あ}いが{面白|おもしろ}い。
examples.english: The back-and-forth between the funny man and straight man is entertaining.

notes:
ぼける is an intransitive ichidan verb with distinct meanings related to mental decline, visual blur, and comedic behavior.

TRANSITIVITY: Intransitive ({自動詞|じどうし}). The transitive form is ぼかす (to blur, to obscure).

KANJI:
- Can be written as {惚|ぼ}ける or {呆|ぼ}ける, but hiragana is most common

SENSE 1 - SENILITY:
- Describes age-related mental decline
- ぼけ{防止|ぼうし} (senility prevention) is a common phrase

SENSE 2 - PHOTOGRAPHY:
- Describes out-of-focus images
- "Bokeh" in photography terminology comes from this word
- Can be intentional (artistic blur) or unintentional (failed focus)

SENSE 3 - COMEDY:
- In {漫才|まんざい} (manzai), the ぼけ says absurd things while the ツッコミ reacts
- Also means to feign ignorance in general conversation

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ぼけが{進|すす}む (senility progresses)
- {写真|しゃしん}がぼける (photo is blurry)
- ぼけとツッコミ (funny man and straight man)

REGISTER: Neutral. Sense 1 may be considered somewhat direct when referring to actual senility.
